Hi Sara / Acme legal team,

Thanks again for the quick review. Attached is our current DPA redline (DPA_v3_Laura_redline.pdf) with two deployment-mode-specific sections called out: 
- Section 5.2: Data residency and routing for Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pools)
- Section 5.3: On-prem / VPC (Private) operational responsibilities and evidence requests

Two asks from your side I want to confirm up front so we can avoid back-and-forth:
1) Subprocessor notification vs prior approval — you requested prior approval for any new subprocessor that will process Acme data under Dedicated. Our standard is notification plus 10-day objection; we are open to expanding to a higher-touch approval flow only for Private deployments where Acme controls the environment.
2) Cross-border transfers — for Dedicated we propose standard SCC-based transfers; for Private (customer-managed VPC/on-prem) we propose a limited-clause that puts the transfer control under Acme's config.

If you can call out the exact language you prefer on subprocessor approvals and the audit scope for Private deployments, we can respond quickly. Marcus and Marissa are looped for legal/ops confirmation.

Thanks,

Laura / Marissa,

Thanks — quick clarifications from our side:
- Subprocessors: Acme's procurement policy requires prior written consent for any subprocessor that stores or indexes PII at rest. For transient KV caches only used for inference within a request, notification is acceptable. Can you map which Redwood subprocessors would have persistent data access in Dedicated?
- Audit rights: for Dedicated we expect SOC2 evidence annually and the ability to request targeted logs. For Private/VPC we need the ability to request configuration evidence and an agreed process for us to run a joint tabletop audit (once per contract year).
- E-sign: Acme prefers DocuSign for signature and asks that the executed DPA produce a signed PDF.

I can have our counsel propose specific language — would Redwood accept a carveout that treats Private deployments like customer-controlled processing where Acme's controls govern data flows?

Best,
Sara

Head of Privacy Ops, AcmeCorp

Subject: RE: DPA negotiation: deployment-specific data handling (Dedicated vs Private)

Sara — thanks for the specifics. I pulled a short table to clarify subprocessor access by deployment mode (quick summary inline):

- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): Redwood subprocessors may have access to persisted logs and storage used for telemetry and debugging. Any subprocessor that can access persisted PII will be listed in our subprocessor matrix; we currently propose notification + 10-day objection but will accept prior approval for named third parties (e.g., analytics vendors).
- Private (Customer VPC / On-prem): Subprocessors are limited — typically only software vendors that integrate with on-prem infra. We recommend Acme maintain separate network controls and KMS; Redwood will not deploy its telemetry collectors into a Private on-prem unless separately contracted.

On audit language: we can provide SOC2 reports and targeted logs for Dedicated. For Private, we can agree to a tabletop exercise and provide configuration attestations, but on-site forensic audits will need a separate SOW.

I'll draft proposed clauses for the subprocessor approval flow and the Private audit process and attach a short redline.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Folks — quick operational note from infra/security:
- KMS: For Dedicated we offer Redwood-managed KMS with customer-managed keys as an opt-in (Key-wrap and HSM-backed options). For Private we require Acme to supply and manage the KMS/HSM.
- Transfer mapping: SCCs will be used for Dedicated transfers where applicable. For Private deployments, no automatic outbound transfer will be initiated by Redwood — any egress is controlled by Acme's network egress rules.

On approval language, our preferred compromise:
- Dedicated: notification + 10 business days to object to a new subprocessor that will persist PII. If Acme objects, Redwood will either remove the subprocessor or suspend processing for Acme while we remediate.
- Private: prior written consent for any subprocessor that will be installed into the VPC or on-prem environment.

We cannot accept unlimited on-site audit rights for Dedicated; we can offer remote log pulls and a joint SOC2 review. For Private, we will agree to a tabletop and configuration attestation; any forensic or intrusive audits require a separate SOW.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Infra Security, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
